key_insight: A task‑aware search and compression of a tiny latent diffusion backbone enables a one‑step super‑resolution model that matches diffusion quality with far fewer parameters and much faster inference.
problem_solved: Diffusion‑based super‑resolution achieves high quality but is too large and slow for practical deployment due to heavy models and multi‑step sampling; TOC‑SR addresses model size and sampling cost while preserving restoration quality.
method: Start from a 16‑channel latent diffusion backbone and identify a task‑optimal compact architecture tailored for SR.
Construct a parameter‑efficient surrogate via targeted compression (e.g., pruning/architecture search) and task‑aware distillation to transfer diffusion priors into a lightweight model.
Convert the compact surrogate into a one‑step SR predictor that eliminates iterative sampling, using loss alignment and perceptual/quality objectives to retain fidelity.
impact: Makes high‑quality diffusion‑level super‑resolution feasible on constrained hardware by cutting model size and latency, enabling real‑time or edge deployment without large quality loss.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side architecture diagram: standard large diffusion pipeline vs TOC‑SR compact latent backbone and one‑step decoder

paper_title: TOC-SR: Task-Optimal Compact diffusion for Image Super Resolution
paper_authors: Sowmya Vajrala, Akshay Bankar, Manjunath Arveti, Shreyas Pandith, Sravanth Kodavanti
